title.narrative: UN GRZ Joint Programme on GBV II
UN GRZ Joint Programme on GBV II

description.narrative: To contribute to strengthening GBV prevention and response systems in Zambia in line with the provisions of the Anti-Gender Based Violence Act.

The Government of the Republic of Zambia-United Nations Joint Programme on Gender Based Violence Phase II (GRZ-UN JPGBV Phase II) has applied to the Embassy for funding of 50 million SEK to carry out the "Strengthening Prevention and Response Services for GBV in Zambia Programme" during the period 2019-2022.
The contribution aims to increase access to and use of quality prevention and response services for gender based violence in Zambia. This is by improving capacity to deliver coordinated GBV services; access to safe shelters; capacity to deliver quality legal services; economic empowerment of GBV survivors and improving multi-sectoral coordination and governance related to GBV in Zambia.
The contribution is a follow up to phase I of the Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ)/United Nations joint programme on GBV. Phase II will again be jointly implemented by the GRZ through the Ministry of Gender and UN led by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), working with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Childrens Fund (UNICEF), International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and the International Labour Organisation (ILO). The contribution will cover fifteen districts of Zambia namely Kabwe, Kalumbila, Solwezi, Kasama, Mansa, Chinsali, Lundazi, Choma, Senanga, Chililabombwe, Lusaka, Itezhi Tezhi, Mumbwa, Mazabuka and Mongu.
The contribution's total budget is approximately 69 million SEK (USD 6,711,169). 50 million SEK (approximately USD 5,100,000) will be funded by Sweden and €1,490,000 (approximately USD 1,600,000) will be funded by Ireland.

Zambiska statens och FNs gemensamma program för att bekämpa könsbaserat våld har ansökt om bidrag till genomförande av programmets andra fas “Strengthening Prevention and Response Services for GBV in Zambia Programme" under perioden 2019-2022.
Insatsen syftar till att öka tillgång till och användning av förebyggande och vårdande tjänster relaterade till könsbaserat våld i Zambia. Detta ska ske genom att förbättra kapaciteten att på ett samordnat sätt leverera tjänster relaterade till könsbaserat våld, öka tillgången till skyddat boende, öka kapaciteten att bistå med juridiska tjänster, öka överlevares eknomiska egenmakt och förbättra den multi-sektoriella samordningen och förvaltningen relaterad till könsbaserat våld i Zambia.
Insatsen är en uppföljning av fas 1 av zambiska statens och FNs gemensamma program för att bekämpa könsbaserat våld. Fas II kommer återigen att genomföras av zambiska staten, genom ministeriet för jämställdhet, och FN genom FNs utvecklingsprogram, UNDP I samarbete med FNs befolkningsfond UNFPA, FNs barnfond UNICEF, FNs migrationsorganisation IOM och den internationella arbetsorganisationen ILO. Insatsen täcker femton zambiska distrikt: Kabwe, Kalumbila, Solwezi, Kasama, Mansa, Chinsali, Lundazi, Choma, Senanga, Chililabombwe, Lusaka, Itezhi Tezhi, Mumbwa, Mazabuka and Mongu.
Insatsens totala budget är ca 69 MSEK (USD 6,711,169), där Sverige bidrar med 50 MSEK (ca 5 100 000 USD) och Irland med €1,490,000 (ca 1 600 000 USD eller ca 19 MSEK).

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

title.narrative: Agreement UNDP Joint Programme on GBV II
Decision on Contribution UNDP Joint Programme on GBV II

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: GBV survivors and persons at risk (including children and adolescents) have increased access to and utilise quality GBV prevention and response services
- As a result of concerted efforts of the Traditional Leadership, Zambia Police Service, Community Neighbourhood Health Watch, Ministry of Education and Ministry of Community Development and Social Services (MCDSS), five girls (three from Misolo and two from Rufunsa villages) were retrieved from early and forced marriages and returned to school. All the five perpetrators were members of the girls communities and the cases are in court except for one where the perpetrator is on the run.
- Four Village Led One Stop Centres (VLOSCs) were in established in the Chiefdoms of Chief Nkula, Chief Mwase, Chief Chanje and Chief Maguya). In these and the two VLOSCs established in 2021 and 2022, in 2023, a total of 2,470 (1765 females, 705 males) GBV survivors accessed services that included psychosocial counselling, basic health services, legal information, economic empowerment, awareness creation on Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV), and referrals to the Victim Support Unit (VSU), health facilities and courts.
- The Programme provided legal services to 1,016 GBV survivors (914 female and 102 male) in collaboration with the National Legal Aid Clinic for Women (NLACW), Women for Change, and the Young Women Christian Association (YWCA). Legal assistance included legal advice, legal information, and legal representation before the Anti-GBV and User-Friendly Fast Track Courts and other courts of law. In the reporting period, 210 cases were filed before the functional six Anti-GBV and User-Friendly Fast Track Courts where Protection and Occupation orders were obtained.
-The Forensic DNA Laboratory at Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital analysed 115 cases, 47 of which were resolved, while 68 are still undergoing analysis. This brings to a total of 145 cases analysed since the commissioning of the DNA Laboratory. The DNA Lab will reduce the number of cases being lost in the justice process due to lack of evidence.
Outcome 2: GBV survivors, those at risk and communities are empowered to break the cycle of abuse
- Following the training of GBV survivors in business skill and disbursement of start-up toolkits, women have started to own businesses in tailoring, poultry and vegetable farming, mobile money vending and selling used clothes. Women have also shown resilience and improved their business enterprise leveraging the economic empowerment trainings conducted in 2021 and 2022. The beneficiaries entrepreneurial skills have also been improved as there is wealth creation at community, household and individual levels and improvements in the culture of savings in selected project sites.
In one community, one of the women had this to say-
"We were very blank when we started our businesses, recalls Ba Nakulu Mpundu. Now our businesses have grown due to the business knowledge and enterprise skills imparted to us by the UN Joint GBV Programme. The growth in businesses have also helped improve our marriage relationships with our spouses and have made us less abused".
- Through Men's Networks, 2,502 men and boys were reached with messages on positive masculinity focusing on boys and men as agents of change in collaboration with the Zambia National Men's Network in Gender and Development (ZNMNGD) and the Young Happy Healthy and Safe.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
